scope: Independent bounded model-only review, no ordinary-UI or human-fun claim; no runtime edits.
status: Bounded independent review complete before publication; remaining author matrix and ordinary UI owned by model/root.
timing: Native .02-second substeps; blind decision cadence .05 seconds, revised L2 also .1 seconds. Reported duration is simulated, not wall-clock.
v1: Map2 and map3 all cores statically no-dig reachable; existing proof includes zero-dig wins. Repeated full floors/long ladders provide shortcuts.

advancedNoDig.method: BFS through unchanged native neighbors on initial topology; directed gravity edges included; no enemy or timer inference.

blindPlanner: Nearest target by native physical shortest route plus up to three legal diagonal dig openings, with no enemy fields or positions read for decisions. Planning treats openings as persistent; native simulation applies actual 5.5s expiry, gravity, guards and collision.

firstDraft.interpretation: Mandatory two-stage dig and one-way descent occur, but the fast route does not require trapping a guard.
Initial guard stayed too far from the upper core loop; this contradicted a strong luring requirement.
Shortest blind bottom-loop route actually meets a guard.

revisedL2.onlyChange: guard initial position 9,11 to 14,7; unchanged map, cores, speed, warning, limits
revisedL2.interpretation: Original blind shortest line now has a real opposing guard. This does not prove every blind alternative must fail or establish human difficulty.

heldDirections.revisionBoundary: Measured first draft before L2 guard initial-position revision; no final-revision blanket claim.

limits: No ordinary UI, true device, touch or human-fun test.
Bounded <=3-opening planner is a counterexample policy, not an exhaustive solver or proof of impossibility.
A blind win is not by itself invalid content; cost and risk are reported.
Blind planner opens topology only for unreachable targets and does not optimize dig shortcuts to an already-reachable core; nearest-core order is bounded, not globally optimal.
Ordinary UI and remaining success matrix belong to root/model author; independent reviewer did not repeat these.

findings: Fixed main/alternate core orders plus current guard-distance-weighted physical paths.
Excavation side chosen using current guard proximity; same-row 2–4-cell threat can trigger a legal dig.
L3 alternate also has a fixed far-side return waypoint; hybrid reactive/path design, not anticipatory strategy.
policySource.decisionFixture: Guard at (4,7) selects opposite dig stand (6,7); guard at (6,7) selects (4,7). Both leave input snapshot unchanged. These are deliberate source-sensitivity fixtures, not naturally reached gameplay.
